unique_findings: Positioning: they describe Sherpas not as another planning app but as an "AI-native operating layer" that standardizes the analytical foundation of advice across intake, modeling, and recommendation drafting — i.e., a horizontal orchestration layer that sits above legacy tools rather than a point-solution.

Document intelligence UX: a text-to-extraction, no-code UI for creating custom extraction rules ("just type what you need") that maps free-text prompts directly to structured extraction schemas — this is a product choice that shifts complexity from engineering to UX and could dramatically reduce onboarding friction.

Pre-trained, domain-specific document library + custom rules: they combine a curated set of pre-trained financial document models (tax returns, brokerage statements, loan agreements) with user-editable extraction rules, implying a hybrid approach (base models + prompt/regex-like overrides) rather than pure black-box ML.

Plain‑English, explainable diagnostics: core product promise is automated, story‑style diagnostics that are structured and explainable, implying investments in deterministic post-processing, templating, and traceability layers (mapping model outputs to audit-ready narrative statements).

Edge/region-first hosting mix: infrastructure references Fly.io and Equinix together — an unusual combo that suggests they're running app/runtime close to users (Fly.io's edge VMs) while relying on Equinix for compliance-grade colocation and data residency. That's an atypical hybrid infra choice for a seed-stage startup.

Enterprise compliance & observability emphasis: explicit SOC 2 pursuit, real-time controls page (trust.sherpaswealth.com), OWASP ASVS adoption, Qualys A for TLS, PFS, and HSTS — shows investment in operational controls and security maturity early on.

Integrated lead intake + automation flow: questionnaire → automatic calendar booking → full financial profile in dashboard shows they've automated several operational touchpoints (data capture, scheduling, first-pass analysis) to reduce conversion friction.

Focus on decision frameworks across domains: they plan to deepen retirement, tax, investment, and risk decision frameworks. That suggests a modularized rules/engine layer that can be extended domain-by-domain rather than one monolithic model.

secret_sauce.core_advantage: A combined stack of domain-tuned AI models (document understanding + financial decision frameworks) integrated directly into advisory workflows so data ingestion, modeling and narrative recommendation are automated and produce explainable, advisor‑voice outputs tied to a firm's own benchmarks and model portfolios.
secret_sauce.defensibility: Medium: defensible because of proprietary labeled financial-doc and planning datasets accrued during enterprise pilots, deep integration into advisor workflows and model portfolios, regulatory/compliance posture (SOC2 readiness) and productized decision frameworks that map to advisor processes. However, components (LLMs, OCR, cloud infra) are broadly available, so long-term defensibility depends on data, integration breadth and enterprise adoption.

competitive_analysis.moat_explanation: Sherpas' moat comes from combining domain-specific AI models, decision frameworks, pre-trained financial document extraction, and deep integrations into advisor workflows plus enterprise compliance posture. Those create switching costs and implementation friction for small competitors. However, major incumbents and cloud providers can replicate parts of the stack (LLMs, OCR) and large incumbents have distribution, making the moat not yet high. Sustainable advantage will require proprietary labeled data from advisors, many integrations, and a growing installed base to create network effects and product configurability unique to large advisory firms.
